<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **35** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7e200b4a68c242afc9f7caf0289e985eff3fcac6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6c5250cbdb420485586b6b642a601ad8565149a0`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/cli/src/utils/collect-docs.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/collect-docs.nav-target.test.ts + packages/cli/src/utils/artifact-packages.ts (`artifactPackages`), packages/cli/src/utils/nav-contribution-groups.ts (`collectNavGroupInputs`), packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts (`composeStacks` step 1/3a, `selectManifest`, `preservePackageEntries`, `assemblePackageBody`, `packagesCarryEveryInputCollection`, `ArtifactPackageSchema`), packages/spec/src/kernel/manifest.zod.ts (`navigationContributions`), packages/spec/src/ui/app.zod.ts (`NavigationContributionSchema`), packages/core/src/stack-collections.ts (`resolveStackCollection`), packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts (D4 read-both door, `unclaimedTopLevel`), packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (`registerApp` step 4b), skills/objectstack-ui/rules/pages.md, content/docs/ui/apps.mdx, docs/adr/0029 D7, docs/adr/0130 D4 and its 2026-09-22 addendum. Face: narrowing (the PR body and the changeset both carry the `no (narrowing)` declaration); the floor is every path outside the prose face, and the changeset is judged under ② only.

Inputs read: card #27343 (body, triage, claim, os-dev-report), PR #27394 (body, file list, net diff against `main` at the merge-base `28872e68d`: 3 files, +49/-2), and the check-runs on the head. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept-set narrowing, the one the card asked for — right.** On a stack that carries `packages[]`, a `type: 'doc'` item in any package body's `navigationContributions` whose `doc` names no doc the artifact carries, or whose `book` names no declared book and no package id, is now refused by `docs/nav-target` through `os build`, `os validate` and `os lint` (`lintDocNavTargets`, `collect-docs.ts` lines 1199-1207 at the head). The runtime registers exactly those bodies' contributions: `resolveArtifactPackageOrder` answers the bodies alone when `packages[]` is present, and `engine.ts` `registerApp` step 4b reads `navigationContributions` off each registered body. The published text already promised this refusal with no single-package limit (`pages.md` line 356: "`os build` refuses a target the package lacks (`docs/nav-target`)"; `apps.mdx` lines 246-248).
2. **Accept-set widening, implied — right, and it is of a dead copy only.** On a stack that carries `packages[]`, the top-level `manifest.navigationContributions` are no longer judged. On every composer-produced artifact that key is `selectManifest(stacks, 'last')`: the last manifest-bearing input's own manifest object, which `assemblePackageBody` spreads into that same input's body, so every top-level contribution IS a body's contribution and is still judged (once; on `main` the owner's copy was the only one judged at all). The one shape that loses a judgment is a hand-written `packages[]` artifact whose top-level manifest carries contributions no body carries. The runtime never registers those: the residual rule (`unclaimedTopLevel`, `packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts`) walks `ARTIFACT_FIELD_TO_TYPE` collections only, and `navigationContributions` is a manifest key, not a collection. `collectNavGroupInputs` made the identical call for the same key with the same reasoning in its docblock. Dropping a judgment of a copy the runtime discards is the lint agreeing with the runtime.
3. **Unchanged population — right.** A stack with no `packages[]`, or with `packages: []`, takes the top-level read exactly as before (`artifactPackages` returns `[]` for both; `collectNavGroupInputs` draws the same `length > 0` line).
4. **Public surface — none moved.** `lintDocNavTargets(stack, docNames)` keeps its signature and export; no new export, no spec or schema change, no `packages/spec` artifact to regenerate. The docblock's "Walked:" sentence now states the new rule.
5. **Test — right and discriminating.** The new case builds the artifact through the real `composeStacks(…, { manifest: 'preserve' })`, pins that the non-owner's contribution is absent from the top-level manifest, and pins three outcomes that differ from `main`: non-owner dead doc (0 issues on `main`, 1 at the head), resolving doc (0 both), both packages dead (1 on `main`, the owner's only; 2 at the head, one per package). The dev's red-first and ablation claims are not re-run here; the logic above is what the verdict rests on.

### ② Semver level

- The changeset bumps `@objectstack/cli` `minor`, carries the `**BREAKING**` banner, a `fix(cli)!:` summary, the `no (narrowing)` declaration and the `narrowed` kind on their own lines, and one ADR-0087 marker reading `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` with its reason. The PR body carries the same two declaration lines plus `Skills-docs: none — …` with a reason that holds on `main` (both cited texts teach the refusal with no single-package limit).
- **The `Clause-②` value and arm are right.** The declaration answers "does this card widen the accept set or enlarge the public surface" (`.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/execution-duties.md`, the claim rules): this diff widens nothing published and narrows a build-time accept set, so `no`; a narrowing is breaking, so the `(narrowing)` arm. `execution-duties.md` states it directly: a card narrowing a published accept set is `Clause-②: no` and owes this review before the queue.
- **The kind and level are right under the repo's rule.** AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3 and the level table in `pr-automation.yml` (maintainer ruling A): "a value refused … is `narrowed`", and a declared kind takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves. A `doc`/`book` value in an authorable `navigationContributions` item that built clean on a multi-package artifact is now refused at the build door — a value refused on what an author writes, in the package whose published source moves. `narrowed` beside `no (narrowing)` is the consistent pairing the level gate and the ADR-0087 gate both read; `Check Changeset` and `Lint & Repo Gates` are green on this head.
- **Precedent PR #27342 (`patch`, `yes (narrowing)`, `none`) is the one out of step, not this PR.** Its diff widened nothing published (a test-only masker fix plus the same class of build-door narrowing), so `yes` declared a widening that did not exist, and `none` sat beside a refused authorable value. Under ruling A the level follows the kind, and for this class the kind is `narrowed`. The dispatch here chose correctly; the precedent is for the dispatching seat to note, not for this PR to mirror. No change owed to this PR.
- The breaking changeset carries its remedy paragraph (no key is removed or renamed, so no FROM → TO mapping is owed), and the ADR-0087 disposition names a category the gate reads.

### ③ Boundary flags

- os-dev-report `open_questions: []`, `out_of_scope_findings: []`. Five deviations, each answered:
  1. Declaration lines differ from the #27342 precedent — answered in ②: this PR's lines are the ones the rule produces.
  2. The PM mechanism hypothesis ("top level when present, else bodies") was falsified and inverted — answered in ④ below: the implemented rule is the right one for a manifest key, and it is the rule the runtime's registration and `collectNavGroupInputs` already apply.
  3. eslint run scoped to `packages/cli` rather than the repo sweep — CI's `Lint · ESLint` is green on this head; nothing owed.
  4. The unit tier, typecheck and first gate run were at `260fe77e0`, before the `origin/main` merge — the merge touched none of the three changed files, and every derived gate family and the dogfood battery were re-run at the head; the head's check-runs are the gate verdicts in any case.
  5. `check:docs-transcript-drift` not derived; no `content/docs/**` file touched — consistent with the three-file list.
- PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no relay-author note owed.
- Observation for the dispatching seat, not a flag on this PR: the runtime's residual rule says nothing about a `packages[]` artifact's top-level `navigationContributions` that no body carries (it registers neither them nor a warning; only `ARTIFACT_FIELD_TO_TYPE` collections are listed). After this PR neither door speaks for that hand-written shape. Pre-existing, out of this card's scope, worth a card under the "absence must be loud" rule if the seat judges the shape reachable.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing against the published spec on `main`: `manifest.navigationContributions` is declared as what a package injects into apps it does not own, "which the runtime merges" (`manifest.zod.ts` lines 971-982; ADR-0029 D7), its items are the ordinary `NavigationItemSchema` set and so admit `type: 'doc'`, and the published docs say the build refuses a dead doc target with no single-package limit. The change takes no declared capability away at the consumer — every contribution the runtime registers on a multi-package artifact is now judged, and nothing the runtime registers is newly refused that the single-package path would have accepted. It makes the spec's own refusal real where the lint had not reached.

"Bodies when `packages[]` is present, else the top level", tried shape by shape against the composer and the loaders:

- **Single package, no `packages[]`** — top-level read, byte-identical path. Holds.
- **Preserve, non-owner contributes** — the top level has no contributions (`selectManifest('last')` picks the owner's); the body read finds one. Holds (tested).
- **Preserve, owner also contributes** — the top-level manifest is the owner's manifest object, spread into the owner's body by `assemblePackageBody`; the body read judges it once, the non-owner's once. Holds (tested).
- **Preserve where the last input has no manifest** — `selectManifest('last')` falls back to the last manifest-bearing input, and `preservePackageEntries` emits a body for exactly the manifest-bearing inputs; a manifest-less input cannot carry a manifest key. Nothing lost. Holds.
- **Preserve yielding one body** (one of two inputs manifest-less) — `packages: [X]`, flattened half kept (`packagesCarryEveryInputCollection` is false below two entries); the body read finds X's contributions, which are the top-level manifest's. Holds.
- **Nested preserve** — an inner artifact's `packages` entries are carried untouched, and its manifest is one of its own bodies' (its `'last'` pick), so the outer top-level manifest is still a body's. Holds.
- **Hand-authored input carrying `packages[]` and a manifest that is none of its bodies** — its manifest is never assembled into a body, so a contribution written there is judged on `main` and not at the head. The runtime never registers it either (`resolveArtifactPackageOrder` answers the bodies alone; the residual rule covers collections, not manifest keys), so the head agrees with the runtime where `main` disagreed. Not a must-fix; the silent runtime drop is the observation in ③.
- **`packages[]` with a body lacking `manifest`, or a `null` entry** — `ArtifactPackageSchema` is strict with `manifest` required; `os build`/`os validate` hand `result.data` (parsed) to `collectAndLintDocs`, while `os lint` hands `normalizeStackInput(config)` (map-to-array normalization and the ADR-0087 conversion pass, before Zod). `artifactPackages` tolerates a missing `manifest` (`?? {}`: no contributions, no throw). A `null` entry would throw on the unparsed `os lint` path, but `collectAndLintDocs` (`declaredPackageEntries`) and the function's own books walk on `main` already call `artifactPackages` over the same list before this read, so the head adds no new throw surface. Holds.
- **`packages: []`** — `bodies.length === 0`, top-level read; the same line `collectNavGroupInputs` draws. Holds.
- **Reconciled preserve composition** (flattened half kept) — the apps walk reads the top-level union (`resolveStackCollection`'s rule, `apps` being a concat collection), the contributions read the bodies (a manifest key whose top level is one package's copy). No double count, no gap; each rule matches its own runtime reader. Holds.
- **Resolution set** — contributed items resolve against `artifactNames` (every doc the artifact carries) and against books plus package ids from the top level and every body, as the apps walk does; a non-owner's contribution may name a sibling's doc and pass, which is the cross-package reading the earlier C2 ruling made ordinary. Holds. (The untouched docblock sentence "against this package's set", line 1198 on `main`, is stale wording from before that ruling; not this diff's, no fix owed here.)

Findings: no must-fix, no should-fix. Two notes carried in ③ (the runtime's silent drop of a hand-written top-level contribution; the #27342 declaration precedent), neither on this diff.
